reading: The UN has warned that the developing El Niño could become exceptionally strong.
The phenomenon originates in the Pacific, where changes in wind patterns allow warmer water to spread eastwards.
Heat released from the ocean into the atmosphere can alter weather patterns far beyond the Pacific.
Forecasters expect unusually dry conditions across substantial parts of South East Asia and Central America.
In contrast, parts of eastern Africa and southern Brazil may receive heavier rainfall.
It could cause disruption to economies around the world.
Governments are preparing through stronger warning systems and advance arrangements for medical assistance.
The WMO is working to ensure that forecasts reach communities exposed to extreme weather.
Australia has introduced warning systems to support responses to marine threats, including risks to fisheries.
The event is unfolding against a background of global warming that could intensify its effects.
